name: Question 4
problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}=4{x}^{2}\sqrt{y},\,y(0)=2
$$

Using the trapezoidal method with step size $Δx=0.5,$ the new value ${y}_{\text{new}}$ is obtained by solving the equation $g({y}_{\text{new}})=0$ at each step. Which of the following is the **general form** of $g({y}_{\text{new}})$ in terms of the new values ${x}_{\text{new}}$ and ${y}_{\text{new}},$ and the current values $x$ and $y?$
worked_solution:
For an initial value problem

$$
{y}^{′}=f(x,y),\,y(a)=c,
$$

the trapezoidal method with step size $Δx$ is given by

$$
Δy=\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{\text{new}}^{′})\cdot Δx,
$$

with ${y}_{\text{new}}^{′}=f({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{\text{new}})$ evaluated at the next $x$ and $y$ values.

In this example, $Δy$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & =\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{\text{new}}^{′})\cdot Δx \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(4{x}^{2}\sqrt{y}+4({x}_{\text{new}})^{2}\sqrt{{y}_{\text{new}}})\cdot 0.5 \\  & ={x}^{2}\sqrt{y}+({x}_{\text{new}})^{2}\sqrt{{y}_{\text{new}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this into ${y}_{\text{new}}=y+Δy,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+{x}^{2}\sqrt{y}+({x}_{\text{new}})^{2}\sqrt{{y}_{\text{new}}},\end{aligned}
$$

and moving all terms to the left-hand side gives the equation

$$
{{{y}_{\text{new}}-({x}_{\text{new}})^{2}\sqrt{{y}_{\text{new}}}-y-{x}^{2}\sqrt{y}}_{⏟}}_{g({y}_{\text{new}})}=0.
$$

Therefore, the general form of the function $g$ for step size $Δx=0.5$ is

$$
g({y}_{\text{new}})={y}_{\text{new}}-({x}_{\text{new}})^{2}\sqrt{{y}_{\text{new}}}-y-{x}^{2}\sqrt{y}.
$$

Question 4
?

Consider the following initial value problem: y′=4x2y,y(0)=2 Using the trapezoidal method with step size Δx=0.5, the new value ynew is obtained by solving the equation g(ynew)=0 at each step. Which of the following is the general form of g(ynew) in terms of the new values xnew and ynew, and the current values x and y?

a
g(ynew)=ynew+(xnew)2ynew−y−x2y
b
g(ynew)=ynew−2(xnew)2ynew−y−2x2y
c
g(ynew)=ynew−(xnew)2ynew−y−x2y
d
g(ynew)=ynew−(xnew)2ynew−y−x2y
e
g(ynew)=ynew−(xnew)2ynew−y−(xnew)2y
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

For an initial value problem y′=f(x,y),y(a)=c, the trapezoidal method with step size Δx is given by Δy=12(y′+ynew′)⋅Δx, with ynew′=f(xnew,ynew) evaluated at the next x and y values.

In this example, Δy is given by

Δy=12(y′+ynew′)⋅Δx=12(4x2y+4(xnew)2ynew)⋅0.5=x2y+(xnew)2ynew.

Substituting this into ynew=y+Δy, we have

ynew=y+Δyynew=y+x2y+(xnew)2ynew,

and moving all terms to the left-hand side gives the equation

ynew−(xnew)2ynew−y−x2y⏟g(ynew)=0.

Therefore, the general form of the function g for step size Δx=0.5 is

g(ynew)=ynew−(xnew)2ynew−y−x2y.
